title: Association between glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist use and peri-operative pulmonary aspiration: a systematic review and meta-analysis
authors: Elkin J, Rele S, Sumithran P, Hii M, Thuraisingam S, Spelman T, et al.
population: 28 observational studies of fasted patients or volunteers using GLP-1 receptor agonists before procedures under anaesthesia or sedation; search to January 2025; no randomised trials were found
funder: The first author was supported by an Australian Government Research Training Program Scholarship; open access publishing was facilitated by the University of Melbourne. No statement on funder role was given.
authorConflicts: Two authors received research support paid to their institutions from Eli Lilly for investigator-initiated studies; one co-authored manuscripts with medical writers provided by Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly; one reported orthopaedic device company fees.
result: In 9 studies of 185,414 patients with 471 aspiration events, GLP-1 receptor agonist exposure was not associated with pulmonary aspiration (odds ratio 1.04, 95% CI 0.87 to 1.25; low certainty). In 18 studies of 165,522 patients with 3831 cases, exposure was associated with residual gastric contents despite appropriate fasting (5.96, 3.96 to 8.98; low certainty). Withholding at least one dose was associated with lower odds of residual gastric contents in 5 studies of 1706 patients (0.51, 0.33 to 0.81; very low certainty).
